checks: Runtime inputs are onboard raw tracks and pose-stale status; no true vessel, target, scenario or outcome access.
Track.confirmed is exactly hits >= TRACK_MIN_HITS; fresh matched free-space tracker updates append the current scan serial.
Only a new finite observed cluster from a fresh matched confirmed track can seed or apply heading memory.
Current valid fits refresh memory without replacing the current view. Finite but rejected fits clear stored memory.
Missing raw IDs, reduced age/hits, and the existing TRACK_MAX_MISSES decision-age limit discard memory; duplicate raw/base IDs reject ambiguity.
Current MotionAxisPerception corrections take priority over remembered heading.
Only existing nonnegative same-source views can have heading replaced; synthetic views, admission, positions, velocities, context and static points remain unchanged.
The base perception is called once, and diagnostics are detached before publication.
hull_heading_memory=False retains the exact parent V16 perception object and delegates action/state behavior; no raw-yaw observer ablation is introduced.

Synthetic tests cover expiry, stale/missed/repeated observations, invalid fits, identity reset/absence, source zero, duplicate IDs, motion-axis precedence, nonmutation, forbidden truth access and disabled delegation.
limitations: A genuinely turning but partly observed target may make a remembered hull axis inaccurate before expiry.
An undetectable same-ID reuse without absence or decreased age/hits remains dependent on the raw tracker's identity assumption.
New-serial/current-cluster freshness depends on the reviewed tracker update invariant; the adapter does not independently compare history serial with tracker._scans.
This is an engineering heading hold, not an uncertainty bound, manoeuvre predictor or safety guarantee.
Source review does not establish episode improvement or absence of regressions.
